subject: CardinalPay API: 504 spike and SLA credit inquiry
messages:
From: Olivia Zhang <olivia.zhang@cardinalpay.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 09:14:22 -07:00
Subject: CardinalPay production: 504 spike (08:37-08:59 PDT) — immediate confirmation & credit path?

Hi Priya / Laura,

We observed a sustained wave of 504s from 08:37 to 08:59 PDT this morning against the Redwood inference endpoint for tenant D-48721. Our checkout traffic incurred ~350 failed transactions and a visible revenue impact; our monitoring exported a CSV with the minute-level 504 counts which I attached (cardinalpay-504-window.csv).

Can you please confirm:
- Whether Redwood saw an outage/degraded window on us-west-2 for our tenant in that interval
- Whether this meets the SLA definition for an availability incident and, if so, next steps for crediting / remediation

We need a prompt acknowledgement and a timeline for evidence and postmortem. If useful I can share packet captures and our request IDs — I’ve also cc’d support+infra for the traces.

Thanks,
Olivia Zhang
SRE — CardinalPay
olivia.zhang@cardinalpay.com

Hi Olivia — thanks for the heads up and for the CSV. I’ve opened an internal incident INF-4721 and looped in Rafael (runtime lead) and Laura (account owner) so we can triage immediately.

What we will do in the next 24 hours:
- Redwood will pull raw traces for tenant D-48721 for 08:20–09:10 PDT and produce an initial impact window verification (timeline + request counts).
- Rafael will run a quick service-side check to determine whether this was a control-plane routing event, autoscaler perturbation, or upstream overload.
- We’ll publish an evidence bundle (redwood-raw-traces-tenant-48721.zip) and a preliminary eligibility assessment for SLA crediting.

Could you confirm whether the CSV covers all affected endpoints (we see both /v1/generate and /v1/chat come through on your side) and attach any PCAPs you have. That will speed verification.

We’ll aim to get an initial verification within 8 business hours and a proposed remediation/postmortem timeslot within 48 hours.

— Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Subject: Re: CardinalPay production: 504 spike (08:37-08:59 PDT) — initial technical readout

Hi Olivia — Rafael here from Runtime. Appreciate the packet capture; I’ve completed an initial pass of the traces and our service telemetry. Preliminary findings:

- We observed a routing imbalance in us-west-2 between 08:38:50 and 08:47:20 where a subset of host pools returned 504s due to an autoscaler eviction storm. The eviction coincided with a heavy short-lived batch of requests from an internal training job unrelated to CardinalPay; autoscaler activity caused a momentary loss of available capacity for certain model-serving shards.
- Total counted failed requests for tenant D-48721 in our logs: 362 (matches your ~350 figure).
- Root-cause candidate: aggressive ephemeral pool scaling + a stale node termination hook that stalled KV-cache rewarm for ~2–3 minutes.

Next steps we propose:
1) We will assemble the full evidence bundle (redwood-raw-traces-tenant-48721.zip) and share the raw time-aligned traces + scaling logs by EOD.
2) We will propose a preliminary SLA credit calculation scoped to the impacted window and per the contract (looking at proportional availability loss).
3) Schedule a 30-minute postmortem review with your infra and our runtime team — suggested slot tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PDT.

For transparency: this appears to be an operational regressional coupling between autoscaler behavior and cache rewarm. We’ll include mitigation actions (safer termination hooks, guardrails on ephemeral training bursts in shared host pools) in the postmortem.

If you want us to proceed with a provisional credit calculation now I can supply a candidate number; otherwise we’ll wait until the evidence bundle is ready.

— Rafael Mendes
Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Hi Olivia — following up with the packaged evidence and our provisional recommendation. We shared REDWOOD-INF-4721 evidence bundle to the Drive link below and attached a short impact summary. Based on the documented window and the contract terms, our provisional credit calculation is a prorated credit equal to 8% of October Hosted usage for tenant D-48721 (we can provide the token-hour math upon request). We’re offering that provisionally while the postmortem completes.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcDeFgHIJk
Postmortem meeting: we’ve proposed Mon Oct 22, 2028 10:00–10:30 PDT for the 30-minute review (invite will follow).

Next steps for you: please confirm you received the evidence bundle and whether the provisional credit calculation is acceptable so we can route billing. If CardinalPay prefers a different allocation method we’ll work with finance ops during reconciliation.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll include a corrective action list and timeline in the final postmortem.

— Priya
